## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

A two-fascicle Suí-period (cataloged as 隋 in the metadata) translation of the *Mahā-megha-sūtra*'s rain-petitioning chapter by **Narendrayaśas** ([那連提耶舍](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%82%A3%E9%80%A3%E6%8F%90%E8%80%B6%E8%88%8D)) — the Northern-Indian (Oḍḍiyāna) translator who served the Northern Qí, Northern Zhōu, and early Suí courts. The text gives the pre-Tang canonical recension of the *qǐngyǔ* sūtra, parallel to but distinct from Amoghavajra's later T989 ([KR6j0176](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6j/KR6j0176)).

**Abstract**

Narendrayaśas (那連提耶舍, 517–589) was an Oḍḍiyāna *trepiṭaka* who arrived in northern China in the late Northern-Wèi / early Northern-Qí period and remained active as an imperial translator across multiple dynastic transitions. He retired to Mt. Tài during the Northern-Zhōu Buddhist persecution and resumed translation activity at Cháng'ān under the Suí emperor [隋文帝](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%9A%8B%E6%96%87%E5%B8%9D) Wéndì in 582. The present *Dàyúnlún qǐngyǔ* translation belongs to his late Suí period (585–589, ending with his death). The text records the Buddha's pronouncement at the *Nanda-Upananda* Nāga-king assembly of the rain-summoning *vidyā* and the procedure for invoking the four classes of Nāga-rulers. It is the principal pre-Tang Chinese witness to the *Mahāmegha-qǐngyǔ* tradition and was the textual base from which Amoghavajra developed his Tang Esoteric T989 retranslation.
